claim: BMP2K has been potentially implicated in endocytosis and cell differentiation but its molecular functions remained unknown.
source: Bone morphogenetic protein 2-inducible kinase (BMP2K) has been potentially implicated in endocytosis and cell differentiation but its molecular functions remained unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge regarding BMP2K prior to this study, drawing from established scientific literature.

claim: BMP2K has longer (L) and shorter (S) splicing variants.
source: We discovered that its longer (L) and shorter (S) splicing variants regulate erythroid differentiation in a manner unexplainable by their involvement in AP-2 adaptor phosphorylation and endocytosis.
evidence: The existence of two splicing variants is stated in the abstract and demonstrated throughout the manuscript with western blots and other experimental data.

claim: BMP2K splicing variants regulate erythroid differentiation in a manner unexplainable by their involvement in AP-2 adaptor phosphorylation and endocytosis.
source: We discovered that its longer (L) and shorter (S) splicing variants regulate erythroid differentiation in a manner unexplainable by their involvement in AP-2 adaptor phosphorylation and endocytosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing effects on differentiation that do not correlate with endocytic functions.

claim: Both BMP2K variants interact with SEC16A.
source: However, both variants interact with SEC16A and could localize to the juxtanuclear secretory compartment.
evidence: This is supported by BioID proximity biotinylation data and co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Both BMP2K variants could localize to the juxtanuclear secretory compartment.
source: However, both variants interact with SEC16A and could localize to the juxtanuclear secretory compartment.
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data showing colocalization with SEC16A and SEC24B in Figure 2C.

claim: BMP2K isoforms constitute a BMP2K-L/S regulatory system that controls the distribution of SEC16A and SEC24B.
source: Variant-specific depletion approach showed that BMP2K isoforms constitute a BMP2K-L/S regulatory system that controls the distribution of SEC16A and SEC24B as well as SEC31A abundance at COPII assemblies.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data in Figure 3 showing differential effects of variant-specific depletion on SEC16A and SEC24B distribution.

claim: BMP2K isoforms constitute a BMP2K-L/S regulatory system that controls SEC31A abundance at COPII assemblies.
source: Variant-specific depletion approach showed that BMP2K isoforms constitute a BMP2K-L/S regulatory system that controls the distribution of SEC16A and SEC24B as well as SEC31A abundance at COPII assemblies.
evidence: This is supported by microscopy data in Figure 3 showing differential effects on SEC31A load at COPII assemblies.

claim: BMP2K-L promotes autophagic degradation.
source: Finally, we found L to promote and S to restrict autophagic degradation and erythroid differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data in Figure 4A showing reduced LC3B-II and accumulated p62 upon BMP2K-L depletion, and autophagic flux analysis in Figure 4C.

claim: BMP2K-S restricts autophagic degradation.
source: Finally, we found L to promote and S to restrict autophagic degradation and erythroid differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by western blotting data in Figure 4A showing increased LC3B-II and reduced p62 upon BMP2K-S depletion, and autophagic flux analysis in Figure 4C.

claim: BMP2K-L promotes erythroid differentiation.
source: Finally, we found L to promote and S to restrict autophagic degradation and erythroid differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4D showing reduced hemoglobin production upon BMP2K-L depletion.

claim: BMP2K-S restricts erythroid differentiation.
source: Finally, we found L to promote and S to restrict autophagic degradation and erythroid differentiation.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4D showing increased hemoglobin production upon BMP2K-S depletion.

claim: Mouse expresses two splicing variants (isoforms) of BMP2K, the longer (BMP2K-L) and the shorter (BMP2K-S), which result from alternative mRNA splicing.
source: According to the UniProtKB database, mouse expresses two splicing variants (isoforms) of the kinase, the longer (BMP2K-L) and the shorter (BMP2K-S), which result from alternative mRNA splicing.
evidence: This claim is based on information from the UniProtKB database.

claim: In isolated mouse fetal liver erythroblasts differentiated with erythropoietin (EPO)-containing medium, mRNA levels of BMP2K-L and BMP2K-S increased gradually, similarly to TFRC.
source: We observed that in isolated mouse fetal liver erythroblasts differentiated with erythropoietin (EPO)-containing medium, mRNA levels of BMP2K-L and BMP2K-S increased gradually, similarly to TFRC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The abundance of BMP2K-L and -S was initially upregulated and subsequently downregulated during erythroid differentiation.
source: While the amounts of TFRC were markedly elevated, the abundance of BMP2K-L and -S was initially upregulated and subsequently downregulated (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The proportion between the intensities of western blotting detection of the two isoforms (L/S ratio) changed with time of differentiation.
source: Noteworthy, the proportion between the intensities of western blotting detection of the two isoforms (L/S ratio) changed with time of differentiation, as BMP2K-S protein was upregulated earlier (the highest levels detected at 24 hr) than that of BMP2K-L (the highest levels detected at 48 hr) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by densitometric analysis of western blotting results shown in Figure 1B.

claim: BMP2K-S protein was upregulated earlier (the highest levels detected at 24 hr) than that of BMP2K-L (the highest levels detected at 48 hr).
source: Noteworthy, the proportion between the intensities of western blotting detection of the two isoforms (L/S ratio) changed with time of differentiation, as BMP2K-S protein was upregulated earlier (the highest levels detected at 24 hr) than that of BMP2K-L (the highest levels detected at 48 hr) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by densitometric analysis of western blotting results shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The levels of BMP2K isoforms were low in the early stages (R0 and R1), the highest in the transitory stages (R2 and R3) and reduced at the last stages (R4 and R5).
source: Consistently with the analysis of heterogeneous cultures (Figure 1B), the levels of BMP2K isoforms were low in the early stages (R0 and R1), the highest in the transitory stages (R2 and R3) and reduced at the last stages (R4 and R5) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data of FACS-isolated erythroblast stages shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The L/S ratio was in favor of BMP2K-S (L/S < 1) in primitive progenitors (R0) but was shifted towards BMP2K-L (L/S > 1) upon differentiation.
source: It was in favor of BMP2K-S (L/S < 1) in primitive progenitors (R0) but was shifted towards BMP2K-L (L/S > 1) upon differentiation, being the highest at R3 (L/S > 2.5) and remaining high at R4 and R5 (L/S ~ 2) when total BMP2K protein levels were again downregulated (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by densitometric analysis of western blotting results shown in Figure 1D.

claim: K562 cells contain much higher amounts of BMP2K than various immortalized, solid tumor or non-erythroid blood cancer cell lines.
source: We found that K562 human erythroleukemia cells contain much higher amounts of BMP2K than various immortalized, solid tumor or non-erythroid blood cancer cell lines (Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data comparing BMP2K levels across cell lines shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In K562 cells the longer isoform (BMP2K-L) appeared as more abundant than the shorter (BMP2K-S).
source: In K562 cells the longer isoform (BMP2K-L) appeared as more abundant than the shorter (BMP2K-S) (Figure 1E,F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 1E, F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, C.

claim: K562 cells have erythroid progenitor-like features and can initiate erythroid differentiation.
source: K562 cells have erythroid progenitor-like features (Andersson et al., 1979) and can initiate erythroid differentiation (Barbarani et al., 2017; Bu et al., 2014; Ma et al., 2013; Wang et al., 2011; Wu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple literature citations.

claim: BMP2K depletion promoted erythroid differentiation of K562 cells.
source: We found that BMP2K depletion promoted erythroid differentiation of K562 cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing elevated expression of erythroid-specific genes (Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D) and increased hemoglobin production (Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).

claim: shBMP2K markedly elevated expression of erythroid-specific genes.
source: shBMP2K markedly elevated expression of erythroid-specific genes (Figure 1G) and potently increased the number of hemoglobin-positive cells under basal culture conditions (by 6-fold) and in the presence of hemin (by 4-fold) (Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: shBMP2K potently increased the number of hemoglobin-positive cells under basal culture conditions (by 6-fold) and in the presence of hemin (by 4-fold).
source: shBMP2K markedly elevated expression of erythroid-specific genes (Figure 1G) and potently increased the number of hemoglobin-positive cells under basal culture conditions (by 6-fold) and in the presence of hemin (by 4-fold) (Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by benzidine staining data shown in Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: BMP2K is a putative endocytic kinase found among interactors of µ2.
source: As BMP2K is a putative endocytic kinase found among interactors of µ2 (Brehme et al., 2009), it could affect erythroid differentiation via regulation of AP-2-dependent CME.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Brehme et al., 2009.

claim: K562 cells had high phospho-µ2 levels that were strongly reduced upon BMP2K depletion.
source: Consistent with its postulated role in phosphorylating the µ2 adaptin at Thr156 (Wrobel et al., 2019), K562 cells had high phospho-µ2 levels (Figure 1E) that were strongly reduced upon BMP2K depletion (Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 1E, F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: BMP2K depletion increased continuous uptake of fluorescently labelled Tf and 10 kDa dextran by K562 cells.
source: However, while the phosphorylation of µ2 was shown to promote endocytosis (Olusanya et al., 2001; Ricotta et al., 2002; Wrobel et al., 2019), BMP2K depletion increased continuous uptake of fluorescently labelled Tf and 10 kDa dextran (a fluid-phase marker) by K562 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3A–E.

claim: shBMP2K increased early (5 min) and steady state (40 min) Tf uptake as well as dextran internalization, all by around 30%.
source: shBMP2K increased early (5 min) and steady state (40 min) Tf uptake as well as dextran internalization, all by around 30% (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3B, C.

claim: shBMP2K led to elevated TFRC protein levels.
source: Consistently, shBMP2K led to elevated TFRC protein levels (Figure 1F) and higher binding of Tf to cell surface on ice (0' in Figure 1—figure supplement 3F,G, empty bars), arguing for a higher number of Tf receptor molecules available on the PM.
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: A pulse-chase uptake assay of the pre-bound Tf showed a reduction of Tf internalization efficiency in shBMP2K-treated cells (down to 62% from 70% in control cells).
source: A pulse-chase uptake assay of the pre-bound Tf showed a reduction of Tf internalization efficiency (% of surface-bound Tf that was internalized at 37 °C) in shBMP2K-treated cells (down to 62% from 70% in control cells) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3H).
evidence: This claim is supported by pulse-chase uptake assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3H.

claim: Within the two variant-specific interactomes, we found proteins involved in vesicular transport or mRNA translation and transport.
source: Within the two variant-specific interactomes, we found proteins involved in vesicular transport or mRNA translation and transport (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by BioID-MS data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Among regulators of vesicular transport found as proximal to both BMP2K isoforms were CME adaptors: NUMB, PICALM, EPS15R, and AGFG1 (HRB).
source: Among regulators of vesicular transport found as proximal to both BMP2K isoforms were CME adaptors: NUMB, PICALM, EPS15R, and AGFG1 (HRB) (Benmerah et al., 1995; Chaineau et al., 2008; Coda et al., 1998; Miller et al., 2015; Santolini et al., 2000; Tebar et al., 1996; Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by BioID-MS data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, along with literature citations.

claim: As proximal to BMP2K-S we also found proteins annotated to ER-Golgi transport, that is SEC16A, SEC24B and ARFGAP1.
source: However, as proximal to BMP2K-S we also found proteins annotated to ER-Golgi transport, that is SEC16A, SEC24B and ARFGAP1 (Watson et al., 2006; Wendeler et al., 2007; Yang et al., 2002; Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by BioID-MS data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, along with literature citations.

claim: SEC16A was detected with the highest MS score among all trafficking regulators identified for BMP2K-S.
source: Of note, SEC16A was detected with the highest MS score among all trafficking regulators identified for BMP2K-S (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by BioID-MS data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: BMP2K-L and BMP2K-S were significantly enriched in EGFP-SEC16A precipitates.
source: Although we repeatedly observed some non-specific co-precipitation of both BMP2K isoforms on agarose resin with EGFP only, they were significantly enriched in EGFP-SEC16A precipitates (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: EGFP-BMP2K-L was enriched predominantly near the PM, where it colocalized with EPS15R.
source: EGFP-BMP2K-L was enriched predominantly near the PM, where it colocalized with EPS15R (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B.

claim: EGFP-BMP2K-S, although also overlapping with EPS15R near the PM, strongly concentrated in the juxtanuclear region positive for SEC16A or SEC24B.
source: EGFP-BMP2K-S, although also overlapping with EPS15R near the PM, strongly concentrated in the juxtanuclear region positive for SEC16A or SEC24B (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Such juxtanuclear localization to SEC16A or SEC24B-positive compartment, however weaker, could also be observed for EGFP-BMP2K-L.
source: Such juxtanuclear localization to SEC16A or SEC24B-positive compartment, however weaker, could also be observed for EGFP-BMP2K-L (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Silencing of the longer variant had no effect on the expression of the shorter, while BMP2K-S depletion only modestly reduced full length BMP2K-L levels.
source: Silencing of the longer variant had no effect on the expression of the shorter, while BMP2K-S depletion only modestly reduced full length BMP2K-L levels (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: shBMP2K-L led to a modest but reproducible increase in SEC16A protein levels, while shBMP2K-S reduced SEC16A protein levels.
source: shBMP2K-L led to a modest but reproducible increase, while shBMP2K-S reduced SEC16A protein levels (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Depletion of all BMP2K isoforms (shBMP2K) lowered SEC16A levels, to the same extent as shBMP2K-S.
source: Depletion of all BMP2K isoforms (shBMP2K) lowered SEC16A levels, to the same extent as shBMP2K-S (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Protein levels of SEC24B were essentially unaffected by depletion of BMP2K variants.
source: By comparison, protein levels of SEC24B, were essentially unaffected by depletion of BMP2K variants (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The regulation of SEC16A protein levels by the BMP2K-L or -S variants was not due to altered gene transcription.
source: The regulation of SEC16A protein levels by the BMP2K-L or -S variants was not due to altered gene transcription. We observed only ~30% downregulation of SEC16A mRNA levels in cells lacking all BMP2K variants (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Depletion of BMP2K-L had no apparent effect on the morphology or staining intensity of juxtanuclear SEC16A compartment but increased integral fluorescence intensity of the dispersed structures.
source: Depletion of BMP2K-L had no apparent effect on the morphology or staining intensity of juxtanuclear SEC16A compartment but increased integral fluorescence intensity of the dispersed structures, arguing for their expansion (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Upon shBMP2K-S, SEC16A staining was diffused with lower intensity of the juxtanuclear compartment and higher intensity of the dispersed structures.
source: Upon shBMP2K-S, SEC16A staining was diffused with lower intensity of the juxtanuclear compartment and higher intensity of the dispersed structures (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: shBMP2K-L reduced integral intensity of the juxtanuclear but not of the dispersed SEC24B structures.
source: shBMP2K-L reduced integral intensity of the juxtanuclear but not of the dispersed SEC24B structures (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D.

claim: Upon shBMP2K-S, SEC24B staining was diffused, with lower intensity of the juxtanuclear and higher of the dispersed structures.
source: Upon shBMP2K-S, SEC24B staining was diffused as it was the case for SEC16A, with lower intensity of the juxtanuclear and higher of the dispersed structures (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, D.

claim: shBMP2K-L did not affect the appearance of dispersed SEC31A structures but decreased the number of juxtanuclear structures and reduced their SEC31A staining intensity.
source: shBMP2K-L did not affect the appearance of dispersed SEC31A structures. However, it decreased the number of juxtanuclear structures (Figure 3D) and reduced their SEC31A staining intensity (mean fluorescence intensity per structure in Figure 3E, hereafter referred to as SEC31A load).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: shBMP2K-S had essentially no effect on the number of SEC31A-positive structures but strongly increased SEC31A load in both, juxtanuclear and dispersed sites.
source: shBMP2K-S, although had essentially no effect on the number of SEC31A-positive structures (Figure 3D), strongly increased SEC31A load in both, juxtanuclear and dispersed sites (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: Upon shBMP2K-L the juxtanuclear SEC24B structures had lower SEC31A load, while upon shBMP2K-S, both juxtanuclear and dispersed SEC24B structures showed elevated SEC31A load.
source: Reassuringly, upon shBMP2K-L the juxtanuclear SEC24B structures had lower SEC31A load, while upon shBMP2K-S, both juxtanuclear and dispersed SEC24B structures showed elevated SEC31A load (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, E.

claim: BMP2K-L positively regulates the abundance and SEC31A load of juxtanuclear COPII assemblies while BMP2K-S negatively regulates SEC31A load of juxtanuclear and dispersed assemblies.
source: Hence, we found that BMP2K-L positively regulates the abundance and SEC31A load of juxtanuclear COPII assemblies while BMP2K-S negatively regulates SEC31A load of juxtanuclear and dispersed assemblies.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the microscopy data presented in Figure 3.

claim: shBMP2K-L reduced, while shBMP2K-S increased, the levels of lipidated LC3B.
source: We observed that shBMP2K-L reduced, while shBMP2K-S increased, the levels of lipidated LC3B (Figure 4A), indicative of inhibited or activated autophagy, respectively.
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Cells lacking BMP2K-L, although having unchanged p62 mRNA levels, showed a strong increase of its protein content, likely due to restrained autophagy.
source: We observed that cells lacking BMP2K-L, although having unchanged p62 mRNA levels (Figure 4B), showed a strong increase of its protein content (Figure 4A), likely due to restrained autophagy.
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data in Figure 4A and qRT-PCR data in Figure 4B.

claim: Cells lacking BMP2K-S, despite a strong increase in p62 mRNA levels, did not accumulate the protein, which could be explained by elevated autophagic degradation.
source: Conversely, cells lacking BMP2K-S, despite a strong increase in p62 mRNA levels (Figure 4B), did not accumulate the protein (Figure 4A), which could be explained by elevated autophagic degradation.
evidence: This claim is supported by western blotting data in Figure 4A and qRT-PCR data in Figure 4B.

claim: In cells lacking BMP2K-L, the accumulation of p62 protein upon bafilomycin A1 treatment was weaker than in control cells, consistent with autophagy inhibition.
source: Consistent with autophagy inhibition, in cells lacking BMP2K-L, the accumulation of p62 protein was weaker than in control cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by autophagic flux analysis data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: In BMP2K-S-depleted cells, stronger p62 accumulation upon bafilomycin A1 treatment confirmed the increased autophagic flux.
source: In turn, in BMP2K-S-depleted cells, stronger p62 accumulation confirmed the increased autophagic flux.
evidence: This claim is supported by autophagic flux analysis data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Silencing of all BMP2K splicing variants using shBMP2K also elevated p62 accumulation upon BafA1 treatment, indicative of increased autophagic flux.
source: Importantly, silencing of all BMP2K splicing variants using shBMP2K also elevated p62 accumulation upon BafA1 treatment, indicative of increased autophagic flux (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by autophagic flux analysis data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: shBMP2K-L impaired whereas shBMP2K-S increased hemoglobin production under basal culture conditions.
source: Consistently, we observed that shBMP2K-L impaired whereas shBMP2K-S increased hemoglobin production under basal culture conditions (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by benzidine staining data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: BMP2K-L-depleted cells poorly upregulated hemoglobin production upon hemin.
source: BMP2K-L-depleted cells also poorly upregulated hemoglobin production upon hemin (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by benzidine staining data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Worse differentiation of BMP2K-L-depleted cells was not associated with reduced transcription of erythroid-specific genes.
source: However, worse differentiation of these cells was not associated with reduced transcription of erythroid-specific genes (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: In cells lacking BMP2K-S, mRNA levels of several erythroid markers were significantly upregulated.
source: In turn, although in cells lacking BMP2K-S, the hemin-induced hemoglobin production was not increased (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), mRNA levels of several erythroid markers were significantly upregulated (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: BMP2K-L, which positively regulates the abundance of SEC31A at COPII assemblies, stimulates autophagy and erythroid differentiation.
source: Collectively, we found that BMP2K-L, which positively regulates the abundance of SEC31A at COPII assemblies, stimulates autophagy and erythroid differentiation, while BMP2K-S, which restricts SEC31A presence at COPII assemblies, limits autophagic degradation and erythroid differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary claim integrating multiple experimental findings from Figures 3 and 4.

claim: BMP2K-S, which restricts SEC31A presence at COPII assemblies, limits autophagic degradation and erythroid differentiation.
source: Collectively, we found that BMP2K-L, which positively regulates the abundance of SEC31A at COPII assemblies, stimulates autophagy and erythroid differentiation, while BMP2K-S, which restricts SEC31A presence at COPII assemblies, limits autophagic degradation and erythroid differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary claim integrating multiple experimental findings from Figures 3 and 4.

claim: BMP2K has been discovered as a transcriptional target of BMP-2 in osteoblast differentiation.
source: It has been discovered as a transcriptional target of BMP-2 in osteoblast differentiation (Kearns et al., 2001) but later identified as an interactor of proteins involved in clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) (Borner et al., 2012; Brehme et al., 2009; Krieger et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kearns et al., 2001.

claim: BMP2K was later identified as an interactor of proteins involved in clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME).
source: It has been discovered as a transcriptional target of BMP-2 in osteoblast differentiation (Kearns et al., 2001) but later identified as an interactor of proteins involved in clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) (Borner et al., 2012; Brehme et al., 2009; Krieger et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Borner et al., 2012; Brehme et al., 2009; Krieger et al., 2013.

claim: The cellular function of BMP2K is ill-defined and none of its phosphorylation targets are established.
source: Up to date, the cellular function of this member of the Ark1/Prk1 family of serine/threonine kinases is ill-defined and none of its phosphorylation targets are established, although it is suspected to phosphorylate the medium (μ2) adaptin of the AP-2 clathrin adaptor complex (Wrobel et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge regarding BMP2K, with a citation to Wrobel et al., 2019.

claim: BMP2K is suspected to phosphorylate the medium (μ2) adaptin of the AP-2 clathrin adaptor complex.
source: Up to date, the cellular function of this member of the Ark1/Prk1 family of serine/threonine kinases is ill-defined and none of its phosphorylation targets are established, although it is suspected to phosphorylate the medium (μ2) adaptin of the AP-2 clathrin adaptor complex (Wrobel et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wrobel et al., 2019.

claim: Recent reports implicated BMP2K in leukemogenesis.
source: Recent reports implicated BMP2K in leukemogenesis (Tokyo Children's Cancer Study Group (TCCSG) et al., 2017; Pandzic et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Tokyo Children's Cancer Study Group (TCCSG) et al., 2017; Pandzic et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2020.

claim: BMP2K was fished out as a putative stimulator of autophagy, potentially required for erythropoiesis.
source: In a study that did not consider its possible endocytic functions, BMP2K was fished out as a putative stimulator of autophagy, potentially required for erythropoiesis (Potts et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Potts et al., 2013.

claim: Clathrin assembles into lattices shaping vesicles transporting cargo from the plasma membrane (PM) or the trans-Golgi network to the endolysosomal system.
source: Clathrin assembles into lattices shaping vesicles transporting cargo from the plasma membrane (PM) or the trans-Golgi network to the endolysosomal system (Robinson, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Robinson, 2015.

claim: COPII vesicles bud at the ER exit sites (ERES) and deliver cargo to the ER-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC) and the Golgi.
source: COPII vesicles bud at the ER exit sites (ERES) and deliver cargo to the ER-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC) and the Golgi (Venditti et al., 2014), while COPI vesicles transport cargo from the Golgi and the ERGIC back to the ER and between the Golgi cisternae (Arakel and Schwappach, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Venditti et al., 2014.

claim: COPI vesicles transport cargo from the Golgi and the ERGIC back to the ER and between the Golgi cisternae.
source: COPII vesicles bud at the ER exit sites (ERES) and deliver cargo to the ER-Golgi intermediate compartment (ERGIC) and the Golgi (Venditti et al., 2014), while COPI vesicles transport cargo from the Golgi and the ERGIC back to the ER and between the Golgi cisternae (Arakel and Schwappach, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Arakel and Schwappach, 2018.

claim: The scission of budding vesicles occurs due to Sar1 GTPase activity which is stimulated by the assembled coat, particularly by the recruitment of Sec31.
source: The scission of budding vesicles occurs due to Sar1 GTPase activity which is stimulated by the assembled coat, particularly by the recruitment of Sec31 (Bielli et al., 2005; Lee et al., 2005; Sato and Nakano, 2005; Townley et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Bielli et al., 2005; Lee et al., 2005; Sato and Nakano, 2005; Townley et al., 2008.

claim: COPII vesicle production is regulated by Sec16 protein by two distinct mechanisms, either by providing a scaffold organizing COPII assembly or by negative regulation of COPII turnover through inhibition of the Sec31 recruitment.
source: COPII vesicle production is regulated by Sec16 protein by two distinct mechanisms, either by providing a scaffold organizing COPII assembly (Bhattacharyya and Glick, 2007; Connerly et al., 2005; Ivan et al., 2008; Martínez-Menárguez et al., 1999; Watson et al., 2006) or by negative regulation of COPII turnover through inhibition of the Sec31 recruitment (Bharucha et al., 2013; Kung et al., 2012; Yorimitsu and Sato, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations describing Sec16 functions.

claim: Autophagosome biogenesis is initiated at the ER and occurs via incorporation of vesicles derived from ERES or endosomal recycling compartment.
